name: OH-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent David Taylor running with $1.1M raised
No Democratic polling or outside spending evident
model.rationale: The R+21 fundamentals, a well-funded incumbent, and no polling or spending suggesting a competitive race all point to a comfortable Republican hold; prediction markets agree at roughly 97% Republican. Nothing in the evidence justifies moving materially from the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic spending or an unexpected scandal involving Taylor could narrow the margin, though the district lean makes an upset very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
OH-02 is a heavily Republican southern Ohio seat where first-term incumbent David Taylor is seeking reelection. The district's R+21 partisan lean, Taylor's roughly $1.1 million in fundraising and $443,000 on hand, and the absence of any general-election polling or outside spending all point to a comfortable Republican hold. Prediction markets price a Republican win at about 97 percent.

Democratic challenger Jennifer Mazzuckelli has no reported fundraising, and no expert raters list the race as competitive. The forecast expects Taylor to win by roughly 19 points, with the main uncertainty coming from the lack of polling rather than any sign of a genuine contest.
